prompt: Standing $50$ ft from the base of a tree, you measure the angle of elevation to the top as $38^\circ$. How tall is the tree? Round to the nearest tenth of a foot.
hint: The $50$ ft on the ground is adjacent to the angle, and the tree height is opposite it.

hints.text: The $50$ ft on the ground is adjacent to the angle, and the tree height is opposite it.

explanation: Angle of elevation is measured up from horizontal, so the $50$ ft ground distance is the adjacent side.
The tree height is opposite, so use tangent: $\tan 38^\circ = \frac{h}{50}$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Read the angle as a slope
steps: $\tan 38^\circ \approx 0.78$ says the line of sight climbs about $0.78$ ft for every 1 ft you move toward the tree.
Over 50 ft of ground, that is $50 \times 0.78 \approx 39$ ft of climb — the height of the tree.
